rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one dominant terraced bar, so it clears the multi-view coherence test. The stepped silhouette is internally consistent and not a random stair-stack; it behaves like a compact landform with one primary mass and subordinate setbacks. The main weakness is programmatic rather than formal: the visible ground response to the verified access edge is modest, with only a small carved corner/edge condition and no strongly public court or undercut. Still, for neighborhood living the mass plausibly supports compact mixed-use/living with upper hierarchy and a terrace-like communal logic, so it passes program fit. The reference set supports terraced neighborhood massing and simple active-edge pavilion behavior, both relevant to the candidate’s language.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus-like and multi-winged than this compact neighborhood building; do not copy the multi-volume dispersal.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, low-rise massing can create a legible communal plateau/courtyard while keeping a strong continuous primary body.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is flatter and more pavilion-like; the candidate’s stepped section is more assertive and needs stronger ground openness.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A calm rectilinear base with a clear entry setback/canopy can support neighborhood-facing public use without overcomplicating the silhouette.

warnings: Parcel containment was treated as satisfied from the visible diagram; no geometry edits proposed because the candidate is already visually coherent.
The access-edge response is weaker than ideal; a deeper notch, courtyard, or ground carve would improve publicness.
Do not read the stepped upper section as a gymnasium or large-span hall; it is only appropriate here as a compact neighborhood mass.
